submissions.findingTextShort: An acute Neuravena crossover trial reported a Stroop-task signal at 1600 mg but not 2400 mg, arguing against a simple more-is-better dose claim.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 21711204 / DOI 10.1089/acm.2010.0450 studied single doses of 0, 1600 and 2400 mg Neuravena oat-herb extract in older volunteers with below-average cognitive performance using a randomized double-blind crossover design. Fewer errors occurred in the color-naming component of the Stroop task after 1600 mg versus placebo or 2400 mg, while resting blood pressure was unaffected. The signal is acute, task-specific and non-monotonic across the tested doses; it cannot support a generic oatstraw cognition claim, a chronic-benefit claim, or a conclusion that higher doses work better.
submissions.populationContext: Older volunteers with below-average cognitive performance in an acute randomized crossover study
submissions.usageContext: Single-dose proprietary Neuravena oat-herb extract; not generic oatstraw, milky-oat tincture or food oats
submissions.safetyContext: Resting blood pressure was unaffected in this acute study; this does not establish broader or long-term safety.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Small study, selected task outcome, acute exposure and a non-monotonic tested-dose pattern limit generalization.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 20-participant acute 800 mg Neuravena study reported faster task performance and ERP changes, but its small sample and manufacturer employment materially constrain certainty.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 34658781 / DOI 10.3389/fnins.2021.748188 randomized 20 healthy participants to acute 800 mg Neuravena or placebo and measured behavioral performance plus event-related EEG potentials during flanker and oddball tasks. The active group showed faster performance without accuracy loss and changes in N2, ERN and P3a/P3b components, while the placebo group did not show the same neurophysiological changes. This is a small acute proprietary-extract study, not evidence that generic oatstraw treats cognitive impairment. Several authors were employed by Frutarom entities associated with the product, so that conflict provenance must remain visible.
submissions.populationContext: Twenty healthy participants in an acute randomized placebo-controlled neurophysiology study
submissions.usageContext: Single 800 mg dose of proprietary Neuravena green-oat herb extract
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Very small sample, acute laboratory outcomes, proprietary preparation and manufacturer-employment conflicts limit certainty and external validity.
